title: Dictionaries and records
goals: Read and update named dictionary fields
Connect a record to a function call
Distinguish missing fields from zero values

prerequisite.prompt: What does remaining(8, 3) return when its body returns capacity - used?
prerequisite.answer: 5; the caller may store or print it.

vocabulary: A mapping from unique keys to values
A name used to look up a value
The error from looking up an absent dictionary key

blocks.text: A fictional cupboard record has a name, capacity and used count. A list asks us to remember positions. Named fields make the intended meaning visible. Our schema requires name as text and capacity and used as nonnegative integers, with used no greater than capacity.

blocks.title: Python 3 code
Follow the evidence
blocks.caption: Read each row from left to right and connect the evidence to the stated rule.

blocks.text: Square brackets look up the value for a key. The quoted key "used" is text; its value is an integer. Assigning to an existing key replaces that field. Other fields remain the same. Dictionary syntax does not enforce our schema: the programmer must check it.

blocks.label: Set used to 12. Predict the returned spaces. Does a used value of 0 mean the field is missing?

blocks.text: cupboard["Used"] raises KeyError here because keys are case sensitive. Correct it to "used". Adding a new field called "Used" would create a second key and leave the original unchanged; it would not repair the intended lookup.
Named fields reduce position mistakes but do not prove that a record is accurate. A capacity of 2 with used of 5 is representable in a dictionary and violates this schema.

blocks.label: A record has capacity 3 and used 4. It gives -1 spaces without an error. Should it be accepted? Explain.

workbook.title: Identify fields
workbook.prompt: For {"name": "Red", "capacity": 9, "used": 2}, state the keys, value of used and remaining spaces.
workbook.answer: Keys name, capacity, used; used is 2; remaining spaces 7.

workbook.title: Trace an update
workbook.prompt: Change the Red record used to 9. State remaining spaces and whether capacity changes.

workbook.title: Repair a lookup
workbook.prompt: The code reads record["Used"] from the Red record. Explain the error and repair it without adding a field.
workbook.answer: KeyError because Used is absent. Use record["used"].

workbook.title: Build a record independently
workbook.prompt: Create a Green record with capacity 15 and used 6. Pass its fields to remaining and store the result. Update used to 10 and repeat. Predict both results.
workbook.answer: Use a dictionary with name Green, capacity 15, used 6; results are 9 and then 5. The second call must read the updated field.

workbook.title: Check the contract
workbook.prompt: A record has capacity 3 and used 4. It gives -1 spaces without an error. Should it be accepted? Explain.
workbook.answer: No. The used count exceeds capacity. Successful arithmetic does not validate the record.

teacher.background: Teach Week 10 as a two-session investigation using fictional data. A fictional cupboard record has a name, capacity and used count. A list asks us to remember positions. Named fields make the intended meaning visible. Our schema requires name as text and capacity and used as nonnegative integers, with used no greater than capacity. Assess the three stated outcomes through the independent task, not by copying the worked result.
materials: Python 3 editor with a fresh local practice file
Paper trace table and the student workbook
Fictional input records from this lesson; no real student identifiers
sessions: Retrieve the prerequisite and explain the purpose in the opening section.
Read the worked example and diagram; ask learners to trace each step aloud.
Complete W1 and W2, then compare predictions with observed results.
Collect the guided prediction before running; discuss a mismatch and its cause.
Retrieve the main rule without showing the previous answer.
Use W3 to diagnose and repair the stated failure; rerun an earlier case.
Collect W4 independently, including code or plan, predictions and explanations, before hints.
Discuss W5 and the exit; use the fresh retry when support was needed.
teacher.guidedAnswer: Spaces are 0. A present used field with value 0 is different from an absent field. Exit: No. The used count exceeds capacity. Successful arithmetic does not validate the record.
misconceptions: A successful run proves the conclusion
